correctness.rationale: Exact Fourier diagonalization of the full 2k dimensional equilibrium Jacobian yields k quadratic mode factors. Complex Schur-Cohn criterion reduces their simultaneous strict stability to the monotone quartic H_k. The minimum cosine has exact ring parity, enabling a unique crossing and explicit factorization in even dimensions. The odd k^-2 coefficient follows from a simple-root implicit expansion; direct implicit differentiation gives strictly positive outward radial speed. No nonlinear critical stability/bifurcation is asserted; a standalone checker passed finite diagnostics.

value.rationale: The source itself motivates the k-dimensional extension. The theorem solves a natural complete sharp local-stability question for every ring size, distinguishes real flip from nonreal oscillatory crossings by parity, gives exact t=3/4 for all even rings and sharp O(k^-2) odd-ring correction, and quantifies why scalar in-phase stability can hide spatially nonuniform instability.
